电解原理：电解氯化铜溶液与饱和食盐水: Electrolysis: Copper(II) Chloride Solution and Brine
同一个直流电源，为什么电解氯化铜溶液得到铜和氯气，电解饱和食盐水却得到氢气、氯气: With the same DC supply, why does electrolyzing CuCl₂ solution give copper and chlorine, while saturated brine gives hydrogen, chlorine and sodium hydroxide?
电解池把电能变成化学能；电源一断，两极都不再产生新物质: An electrolytic cell turns electrical energy into chemical energy; cut the power and neither electrode makes anything new
阴离子向阳极、阳离子向阴极；电子只在外电路走，不进溶液: Anions go to the anode, cations to the cathode; electrons travel only in the external circuit, never through the solution
阳极 Cl⁻ 先失电子，阴极 Cu²⁺ 或 H⁺ 先得电子——产物就这么定了: At the anode Cl⁻ loses electrons first; at the cathode Cu²⁺ or H⁺ gains electrons first. That fixes the products
Q = I·t；每 2 mol 电子出 1 mol Cu（或 H₂）、同时出 1: Q = I·t; every 2 mol of electrons gives 1 mol Cu (or H₂) and 1 mol Cl₂
整体 · 一张电化学实验台上并排两台电解池，通同样的电、看不同的产物: Overview · two electrolytic cells side by side on one bench, the same current, different products
换电解质、拨阳极、调电流和时间，两极的产物与读数一起变: Change the electrolyte, swap the anode, adjust current and time, and the products and readings at both electrodes change together
全对！电解池的四件事：阳极氧化、阴极还原，阴离子去阳极、阳离子去阴极，谁容易放电: All correct! Four facts about electrolytic cells: oxidation at the anode, reduction at the cathode; anions go to the anode, cations to the cathode; whichever discharges most easily gives the product; and the amount depends only on charge.

电解池：电能 → 化学能（电极反应 · 电极材料 · 离子导体 · 电子导体）: Electrolytic cell: electrical energy → chemical energy (electrode reactions · electrode materials · ionic conductor · electronic conductor)
两台电解池 · 一张实验台 · 全程不换场景: Two cells · one bench · no scene change
两个实验回答的是同一个问题：通同样的电，不同的溶液里谁先放电。: Both experiments answer the same question: with the same current, which species discharges first in different solutions.
两台池子的对照就摆在同一屏上，一眼能比。: The two cells are side by side on one screen so you can compare at a glance.
界面上的电流、时间、产物量都是课件设定（示意读数），教材只说「25% 溶液」「覆: Current, time and product amounts on screen are lesson settings (illustrative readings); the textbook only says "25% solution", "covered with a layer of red copper" and "the paper turns blue".
去掉这一步：学生把两个实验当成两件互不相干的事，不知道它们共用一套「电荷守恒」的: Skip this step and students treat the two experiments as unrelated, not seeing they share one "charge conservation" calculation.
常考：电解池的四要素（电极反应、电极材料、离子导体、电子导体）；电解池与原电池的: Common exam topic: the four elements of an electrolytic cell (electrode reactions, electrode materials, ionic conductor, electronic conductor); the direction of energy conversion in electrolytic vs galvanic cells.
电解池是把电能直接转化为化学能的装置：使电流通过电解质溶液，在阳极、阴极引起氧化: An electrolytic cell converts electrical energy directly into chemical energy: passing current through an electrolyte solution causes redox reactions at the anode and cathode (textbook wording).

把「接通直流电源」打开，盯住两根石墨棒：哪一根盖上了红色的铜、哪一根在冒气泡、试: Turn on "Connect DC supply" and watch the two graphite rods: which one gets coated with red copper, which one bubbles, and how the paper changes
与电源负极相连的那根（左腿，阴极）渐渐盖上一层红色的铜；与正极相连的那根（右腿，: The rod connected to the negative terminal (left leg, cathode) gradually gets a coat of red copper; the rod connected to positive (right leg, anode) bubbles; the moist starch-iodide paper at the anode turns blue. Main reading 0.00 → 0.20 A; cathode copper 4.0 mg, anode Cl₂ 1.5 mL (60 s)
25% CuCl₂ 溶液 · 两根石墨棒 · 接通直流电源: 25% CuCl₂ solution · two graphite rods · DC supply on
红色的是铜，从溶液里的 Cu²⁺ 变来，不是石墨棒变了颜色。: The red is copper, formed from Cu²⁺ in the solution; the graphite rod didn't change color.
气泡是氯气：有刺激性气味，能把碘化钾氧化出碘，淀粉遇碘变蓝——试纸变蓝就是氯气的: The bubbles are chlorine: it has a pungent smell and oxidizes iodide to iodine, which turns starch blue. The blue paper is the evidence for chlorine.
「阳极 / 阴极」说的是氧化 / 还原，跟「正极 / 负极」是两套名字（练习 4: "Anode / cathode" refer to oxidation / reduction, a different pair of names from "positive / negative" (the wrong option in exercise 4 trips on this).
去掉这一步：学生会把「阴极」当成电源负极本身。: Skip this step and students mistake the "cathode" for the supply's negative terminal itself.
高频：电解 CuCl₂ 溶液的电极反应与总反应；现象怎么写；怎样检验阳极气体。: Frequently tested: electrode and overall reactions for electrolyzing CuCl₂ solution; how to describe the observations; how to test the anode gas.
通电后 CuCl₂ 溶液在阳极、阴极分别发生氧化、还原反应，生成了 Cu 和 C: With current on, oxidation and reduction occur at the anode and cathode of the CuCl₂ solution, producing Cu and Cl₂: anode 2Cl⁻ − 2e⁻ = Cl₂↑ (oxidation), cathode Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ = Cu (reduction), overall Cu²⁺ + 2Cl⁻ =electrolysis= Cu + Cl₂↑ (textbook wording).
A2.2、A2.3、A2.5、A2.8、B2.1 标准值表 2、D8: A2.2, A2.3, A2.5, A2.8, B2.1, standard values table 2, D8
通得更久、或者把电流调大，为什么产物就更多？多了多少？: Why do you get more product if you run longer or raise the current? How much more?
把通电时间从 60 s 拖到 300 s 以上，看阴极的铜和阳极的氯气怎样一起长: Drag the electrolysis time from 60 s to over 300 s and watch the cathode copper and anode chlorine grow together; then go back and set the current to 0.40 A to compare
0.20 A 下：60 s → 铜 4.0 mg / Cl₂ 1.5 mL；30: At 0.20 A: 60 s → copper 4.0 mg / Cl₂ 1.5 mL; 300 s → 19.8 mg / 7.6 mL; 600 s → 39.5 mg / 15.2 mL; 1800 s → 118.6 mg / 45.7 mL. Doubling the current (0.40 A · 600 s) → 79.0 mg / 30.5 mL, exactly twice. The curve is a straight line through the origin
产物不是「通得越久越深」那种模糊趋势，而是一条直线：时间加倍、产物加倍。: The yield isn't a vague "the longer, the more" trend but a straight line: double the time, double the product.
电流加倍、同样的 600 s，产物也加倍——电量才是那个「账」。: Double the current for the same 600 s and the product also doubles: charge is what keeps the books.
25% CuCl₂ 溶液很浓，600 s 只让 c(Cu²⁺) 降 1.7 %，: 25% CuCl₂ solution is very concentrated, so 600 s only lowers c(Cu²⁺) by 1.7 % and the color barely lightens. That's why the textbook only has you look at the red copper and the test paper.
去掉这一步：学生以为产物量靠「感觉」，不会用 Q = I·t 去算，一考计算题就: Skip this step and students think yields are guesswork, can't calculate with Q = I·t, and fail calculation questions.
高频：电解的计算（电量 → 产物质量 / 体积）；两极产物的物质的量关系；为什么: Frequently tested: electrolysis calculations (charge → product mass / volume); the mole relationship between the two electrode products; why the solution's color barely changes. Gas volumes use 25 °C, Vm = 24.5 L/mol; the textbook's STP value is 22.4 L/mol, so checking with 22.4 gives 8.6 % less than shown here.
通过的电荷量 Q = I·t 决定产物量：每 2 mol 电子在阴极析出 1 m: The charge passed, Q = I·t, determines the yield: every 2 mol of electrons deposits 1 mol Cu at the cathode and releases 1 mol Cl₂ at the anode (each of the textbook's two electrode reactions is 2e⁻ per particle).
A2.5、A4.4、B2.1 算子 2–4、标准值表 2–9、D2: A2.5, A4.4, B2.1 operators 2–4, standard values tables 2–9, D2
「通电时离子改作定向运动」——到底谁往哪边走？电子又走哪儿？: "With current on, the ions move in a definite direction." So who goes where, and where do the electrons go?
看放大窗里 Cu²⁺ 与 Cl⁻ 各往哪条腿走、导线里的电子箭头指向哪（再回去把: In the magnified window, see which leg Cu²⁺ and Cl⁻ each head for and which way the electron arrow in the wire points (then go back and switch the power off to look again)
放大窗里 Cu²⁺（蓝绿）朝左腿（阴极）、Cl⁻（黄绿）朝右腿（阳极），两根箭头: In the magnified window Cu²⁺ (blue-green) heads for the left leg (cathode) and Cl⁻ (yellow-green) for the right leg (anode), so the two arrows point opposite ways; the electron arrow appears only in the wire, pointing from the supply's negative terminal to the cathode, and no electrons run through the solution. Switch off and all three sets of arrows stop
阴离子 → 阳极 ｜ 阳离子 → 阴极（电子只在外电路）: Anions → anode | cations → cathode (electrons only in the external circuit)
示意放大 · 通电前后离子移动（教材图 4-10）· 正在看：① 电解 CuCl: Magnified view · ion movement before and after switching on (textbook Fig. 4-10) · now viewing: ① Electrolysis of CuCl₂ solution
溶液里的导电靠离子搬家，不是电子在溶液里跑。: Conduction in the solution is ions moving, not electrons running through the solution.
阳离子朝阴极、阴离子朝阳极——两根箭头一定反向，画成同向就错了。: Cations go to the cathode and anions to the anode, so the two arrows must point opposite ways; drawing them the same way is wrong.
电子只在导线里走，从电源负极进阴极；进到阴极以后，这条「接力棒」交给 Cu²⁺: Electrons travel only in the wire, from the negative terminal into the cathode; once there, the "baton" is handed to Cu²⁺.
去掉这一步：学生会画「电子从阳极穿过溶液到阴极」，整道原理图题就废。: Skip this step and students draw "electrons from the anode through the solution to the cathode", ruining the whole diagram question.
高频：画电解池原理示意图（教材思考与讨论就是这道题）；电子流向与离子迁移方向的区: Frequently tested: drawing the principle diagram of an electrolytic cell (the textbook's think-and-discuss question); the difference between electron flow and ion migration.
通电时自由运动的离子改作定向运动：阴离子向阳极迁移、阳离子向阴极迁移；电子在外电: With current on, freely moving ions move in a definite direction: anions migrate to the anode and cations to the cathode; electrons travel in the external circuit from the supply's negative terminal to the cathode and don't enter the solution (textbook wording).
同样是石墨电极、同样的电流，换成饱和食盐水，阴极跑出来的为什么不是钠？: Same graphite electrodes, same current. Switch to saturated brine, and why isn't it sodium that comes out at the cathode?
把「电解质」从 ① CuCl₂ 溶液拖到 ② 饱和食盐水，看阴极产物变成了什么、: Drag "Electrolyte" from ① CuCl₂ solution to ② saturated brine, and see what the cathode product becomes and how much gas each electrode gives
主读数仍是 0.20 A，但产物全变了：阴极冒出氢气 H₂ 15.2 mL（不是: The main reading is still 0.20 A, but all the products change: the cathode gives hydrogen H₂ 15.2 mL (not sodium), and the anode gives Cl₂ 15.2 mL, a gas ratio of exactly 1 : 1; NaOH builds up in the solution and the cathode region turns alkaline. Before switching on, the solution has 4 kinds of ions: Na⁺, Cl⁻, H⁺, OH⁻
放电顺序：阳极 Cl⁻ 比 OH⁻ 易失电子 → 出 Cl₂（不是 O₂）；阴极: Discharge order: at the anode Cl⁻ loses electrons more easily than OH⁻ → Cl₂ (not O₂); at the cathode H⁺ gains electrons more easily than Na⁺ → H₂ (not Na).
Na⁺ 留在溶液里，和阴极留下的 OH⁻ 组成 NaOH——氯碱工业要的烧碱（工: Na⁺ stays in solution and pairs with the OH⁻ left at the cathode to form NaOH, the caustic soda the chlor-alkali industry wants (made industrially in ion-exchange membrane cells).
两极各是 2 个电子一个粒子，所以体积比恒为 1 : 1（体积按 25 ℃、Vm: Each electrode takes 2 electrons per particle, so the volume ratio is always 1 : 1 (volumes at 25 °C, Vm = 24.5 L/mol; the textbook's STP value 22.4 L/mol gives 8.6 % less).
去掉这一步：学生会写「得 Na 和 O₂」。: Skip this step and students write "gives Na and O₂".
高频：电解饱和食盐水的电极反应、总反应、产物；为什么阴极不出钠、阳极不出氧气。: Frequently tested: electrode reactions, overall reaction and products of electrolyzing saturated brine; why the cathode doesn't give sodium and the anode doesn't give oxygen.
阳极 Cl⁻ 比 OH⁻ 容易失电子、阴极 H⁺ 比 Na⁺ 容易得电子，所以产: At the anode Cl⁻ loses electrons more easily than OH⁻, and at the cathode H⁺ gains electrons more easily than Na⁺, so the products are Cl₂, H₂ and NaOH: 2Cl⁻ − 2e⁻ = Cl₂↑, 2H₂O + 2e⁻ = H₂↑ + 2OH⁻, overall 2Cl⁻ + 2H₂O =electrolysis= Cl₂↑ + H₂↑ + 2OH⁻ (textbook wording).
A2.10、A2.11、A5.3、A1.3、B2.1 标准值表 10–11、D3: A2.10, A2.11, A5.3, A1.3, B2.1, standard values tables 10–11, D3
阴极那根棒周围，为什么滴一滴酚酞就红了？: Why does the solution around the cathode rod turn red with a drop of phenolphthalein?
这一台开始时还没滴酚酞——先看看现在只有气泡的样子，再往阴极区滴几滴酚酞: This cell starts without phenolphthalein. Look at it now with just the bubbles, then add a few drops of phenolphthalein to the cathode region
没滴酚酞时只看到两极冒气泡、看不出碱；滴了以后阴极（左腿）附近的溶液变红，并向外: Without phenolphthalein you only see bubbles at both electrodes, with no sign of alkali; once added, the solution near the cathode (left leg) turns red and slowly spreads (cathode region c(OH⁻) = 82.9 mmol/L). For contrast, drag the electrolyte back to ① CuCl₂ solution and add the same phenolphthalein: no red
饱和食盐水 · 阴极区滴酚酞（对照：CuCl₂ 体系滴了不红）: Saturated brine · phenolphthalein at the cathode (control: no red in the CuCl₂ system)
变红不是「酚酞和盐反应」，是阴极反应把 OH⁻ 攒下来了。: The red isn't "phenolphthalein reacting with salt"; the cathode reaction is building up OH⁻.
红只在阴极附近慢慢扩散，不是整管一起红。: The red spreads slowly only near the cathode; the whole tube doesn't turn red at once.
同一个酚酞，滴在 CuCl₂ 体系里不红（Cu²⁺ 先放电，不产生 OH⁻），这: The same phenolphthalein stays colorless in the CuCl₂ system (Cu²⁺ discharges first, so no OH⁻ forms). This contrast shows that "who discharges first decides the product".

关于电解池的阳极和阴极，下列说法正确的是: Which statement about the anode and cathode of an electrolytic cell is correct?

阳极与电源正极相连，发生氧化反应: The anode connects to the supply's positive terminal and undergoes oxidation
阴极与电源正极相连，发生氧化反应: The cathode connects to the supply's positive terminal and undergoes oxidation
阳极和阴极都发生还原反应: Both the anode and cathode undergo reduction

The wrong option in the textbook's practice question 4 is "oxidation occurs at the cathode". Step 2 of this lesson: the anode (right leg, positive) gives chlorine, the cathode (left leg, negative) deposits copper (matching the layout of textbook Fig. 4-9).

电子只在外电路从电源负极流向阴极，溶液中阴离子向阳极、阳离子向阴极迁移: Electrons flow only in the external circuit from the supply's negative terminal to the cathode; in the solution anions migrate to the anode and cations to the cathode
电子在溶液中从阴极跑向阳极，阴离子向阴极迁移: Electrons run through the solution from the cathode to the anode, and anions migrate to the cathode
电子和离子都只在溶液中运动: Both electrons and ions move only in the solution

The magnified window in step 4 draws exactly this.
